description:
FILED s463av from the #981 profile of the `slices` bench row — the residue
that task measured and did not take.

`@a[1..5]` lowers to `(p-aslice @a (p-.. 1 5))` and `@h{@k}` to
`(p-hslice %h @k)`, so `%p-flatten-slice-args` is handed a ONE-element &rest
list whose single element is a vector.  It answers with

    (loop for arg in args
          if (and (vectorp arg) (not (stringp arg))) append (coerce arg 'list)
          ...)

i.e. it allocates a fresh CL list of the indices on every slice, which the
caller then walks once with `dolist` and drops.

MEASURED (same sb-sprof run as #981, N = 1.5e6, 1435 samples, this tree):

    sb-kernel:vector-to-list    2.2 % self / 2.6 % total
    sb-impl::copy-list-to       2.1 % self
    ------------------------------------------------------
    slice-argument list building  ~5 % of the row

for a row whose whole PCL side is 0.20 s against perl's 0.07 s.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX, and why it is not a two-line fast arm.  SIX callers share
the helper — p-aslice, p-hslice, p-kv-hslice, p-kv-aslice, p-delete-hash-slice,
p-delete-array-slice (plus the two KV/delete array twins) — and the helper is
the ONE place the "a range vector is many indices, a string is one" rule lives.
That rule was itself the fix for a real bug (`p-aslice` used to explode "12"
into #\1 #\2, and the two array deletes used to take a range vector as ONE
index).  So adding a fast arm in the two hot callers duplicates the rule into
three places — rule 11's hard stop.  The change that keeps one mechanism is a
REPRESENTATION change: have the helper answer a VECTOR (returning its argument
unchanged in the single-vector case, which is the allocation-free path), and
move all six callers from `(length flat)` + `dolist` to `(length v)` +
`dotimes`.  They already size their result with `(length flat)`, so half the
change is already written.

TWO THINGS TO CHECK BEFORE SHIPPING IT, both of which the aliasing semantics
make non-obvious:

 1. Returning the caller's OWN vector means the slice loop iterates a live
    container.  `%p-alias-aelem` PROMOTES a raw slot to a box as it goes, so
    `@a[@a]` would read index j out of a slot that promotion has since
    rewritten.  Promotion preserves the VALUE (a box around the same number,
    which to-number reads identically), so this looks safe — but probe it
    against perl rather than reasoning about it, together with `@h{@k}` where
    @k is the hash's own keys.

 2. `%p-flatten-slice-args` is declaimed INLINE and its callers are &rest
    functions; check the &rest list itself is not the allocation that dominates
    (measure with one argument and with three).

EXPECTED PRIZE: ~5 % of `slices` (3.05x), less elsewhere.  Small — file it as a
filler, not a session.

SHIPPED s464ax (round 22 PERF slot, 2026-09-02), on `80b715c`.

WHAT WAS DONE, exactly as the task's "representation change" sketch: the
helper answers a SIMPLE-VECTOR **and a COUNT** (two values), and in the
single-vector case the vector is the argument's OWN backing store via
`%p-vec-data`, so the common slice allocates nothing here at all.  All eight
callers moved from `(length flat)` + `dolist` to `n` + `dotimes` + `SVREF`.
One caller cannot take two values â the list-assign LHS macro, whose `let*`
bindings are generated â and gets the thin wrapper `%p-slice-args-vector`,
which is the only place that ever copies for shape.

THE COUNT IS NOT COSMETIC.  A Perl array's backing simple-vector is its
CAPACITY: `my @k = (0..9); pop @k; pop @k;` is 8 entries in a 10-slot store,
so a caller that took `(LENGTH store)` would slice TEN.  Inverse-guard
measured (the count replaced by the capacity): ten of eleven capacity-probe
rows change and three guard rows fail.

THE TASK'S CHECK 1 (aliasing), MEASURED not reasoned.  Reading a live
container is safe â `%p-alias-aelem`'s promotion preserves the value, and
`@a[@a]` / `@h{@k}` with @k the hash's own keys are probe rows that agree with
perl before and after.  But the two array DELETES *write* the array they are
indexing by, and perl evaluates the index list onto the stack before the first
store, so they snapshot on `(eq flat (%p-vec-data a))`.  **The obvious probe
does not discriminate**: `delete @s[@s]` on `(2,1,0)` answers `0,1,2|0` either
way.  On `(1,2,0)` it does â without the snapshot the second index is read out
of the slot the first store emptied, giving `2,1,U|3` where perl says
`2,0,1|0` (and the KV twin `1,2,0,1,0,U|3` vs `1,2,2,0,0,1|0`).  Both
spellings are guard rows.

THE TASK'S CHECK 2 (the &rest list), ANSWERED NO.  In the post-fix sb-sprof
report `LISTIFY-&REST` + `listify_rest_arg` together are **1 sample of 1308**
(0.0 % self, 0.1 % total).  The &rest consing is not the allocation that
dominates, so NO `dynamic-extent` declaration was added â do not re-derive
this.

MEASURED.  sb-sprof, N = 1.5e6, same box, before/after: total sampling time
0.686 s (1372 samples) -> 0.654 s (1308); `sb-kernel:vector-to-list` (1.7 %
self / 2.0 % total) and `sb-impl::copy-list-to` (2.6 % / 2.8 %) are ABSENT
from the whole flat report afterwards.

Bench, interleaved best-of-5 A/B (`BENCH_RT_B`), A = this tree, B = main
`80b715c`, positive = B slower = the change helps; alternated with a CONTROL
A/B of A against a BYTE-IDENTICAL COPY of A so both see the same box (1-min
load 0.1-1.0):

    row          control (3 runs)       A/B (4 runs)
    slices       -0.6 -1.7 +0.1         +5.8 +5.8 +6.4 +5.0    <- every run outside the band
    sliceasgn    +3.2 -1.3 -2.0         -1.0 +0.2 +0.3 -0.0
    arrhash      -1.3 +0.4 -1.1         +0.5 -0.5 +1.0 +2.0
    arrfill      -1.0 +1.5 -1.7         +0.3 -0.7 +0.4 -0.7
    listcopy     +0.0 +4.2 +0.1         -0.1 +0.2 -0.2 -0.0
    feread       +1.7 +0.3 +0.3         +2.2 +12.6 +0.8 +2.4   (one outlier; no slice on this row)
    feread2      +1.5 -1.1 +1.5         +1.7 +3.2 +1.3 +1.5

PCL absolute for `slices`: 0.1878-0.1924 s (A) vs 0.2002-0.2012 s (B), perl
0.0656-0.0681 â the row reads **2.78-2.92x** here against Â§0.2f's 3.02x, i.e.
**-5.5 %**, which is the ~5 % this task predicted.  `sliceasgn` does not move
and that is expected: a list-assign LHS slice goes through the wrapper.

LEGS.  Paren check balanced; gate 193 files / 6542 rows, only the 13 pclxs xs
rows failing; full sweep TOTAL passing 18346 (+0), GATE clean, 0 new / 0
fixed, drops 5 = census; companion `op/ --quick --jobs 4`; PCL_OPT=none runs
the 50-row probe battery byte-identically.  Guard `Pl/t/slice-args-01.t`
(15 rows, 4.7 s -> 2.1 s warm), inverse-verified in BOTH directions.
Record: `docs/faster-codegen-suggestions.md` Â§0.2g.

RESIDUE ON THE ROW, unchanged: **#982** key stringification (~6 % here) and
the ~23 % that is the `equal` hash table itself.

TWO PRE-EXISTING DIVERGENCES the probe battery found (both reproduce on
`80b715c`, both FILED not fixed): **#1010** (perl vivifies a missing hash key
when a slice element is ALIASED) and **#1011** (`%a[-1]` yields the index as
written in perl, normalised in PCL).

ONE THING NOT DONE, and why: the array-slice LHS arm of the list-assign macro
uses a DIFFERENT helper, `%p-flatten-list`, where the hash-slice arm uses this
one.  Whether they agree on every input was not measured and is not this
task's scope â but two flatteners for the same job in adjacent arms of one
macro is the exact shape #394 was.  Worth a look.


=== FABLE REVIEW + MERGE (s464, 2026-09-02) === diff read; probes vs perl 5.40.3 on both PCL_OPT paths (ovl.pl 37 rows for #972/#987: 33 identical, the 4 diffs are the declined #960(a) refusal); rebased and merged ff into main (round 22: AW 3d666ea, AX 300d47f); legs on the final tree in DECIDED s464 round-22 record.
subject: Perf: %p-flatten-slice-args builds a throwaway LIST on every slice (~5 % of the `slices` row) — the single-vector case, which is every slice the corpus writes, could iterate the argument directly
